mapping.name: Uzrah's Palace
mapping.environment: Ancient palace ruins, partially collapsed, haunted by an efreet
mapping.description_long: The crumbling palace of a legendary vizier, now haunted by a capricious efreet. The White Shark of Basra has claimed it as the site for his treasure distribution. The ruins are filled with traps, monsters, and the remnants of ancient magic.

mapping.name: The Gate Hall
mapping.environment: Grand entrance hall, 60-foot ceilings, crumbling pillars
mapping.description_long: The main entrance to the palace. Massive stone doors stand partially open, revealing a hall lined with crumbling pillars. Faded murals depicting ancient victories cover the walls.

mapping.name: The Upper Level
mapping.environment: Palace upper floors, guest quarters, audience chambers
mapping.description_long: The upper floors of the palace, once reserved for honored guests. Now occupied by the White Shark's crew. Dusty tapestries and broken furniture litter the corridors.

mapping.name: The Lower Level
mapping.environment: Underground chambers, treasury vaults, ancient laboratories
mapping.description_long: The basement levels of the palace, where the vizier kept his most precious treasures and conducted his arcane experiments. Dark, cramped, and filled with ancient traps.

mapping.name: The Builder Tunnels
mapping.environment: Narrow service tunnels, connecting various parts of the palace
mapping.description_long: A network of narrow tunnels used by the palace builders and servants. Now home to various creatures and tunnel dwellers.

mapping.name: The Treasure Hall
mapping.environment: Massive vaulted chamber, filled with ancient treasure chests
mapping.description_long: The grand hall where the White Shark plans to distribute his treasure. Piles of gold, gems, and artifacts fill the room. The efreet watches from the shadows, waiting for the right moment to strike.

mapping.name: The Banquet Hall
mapping.environment: Long dining hall, tables set for a feast that never ended
mapping.description_long: A grand dining hall where ghostly servants still tend to a feast that was interrupted centuries ago. The food is dust, the wine is vapor, but the servants remain.

mapping.name: Gate Hall Ambush
mapping.setup: As the party enters the Gate Hall, giant cobras descend from the crumbling ceiling.
mapping.tactics: The cobras attack from above, using surprise to gain advantage. They target the weakest-looking party member first.

mapping.name: Upper Level Patrol
mapping.setup: A patrol of three pirates rounds the corner, weapons drawn.
mapping.tactics: The archer fires from behind while the others engage in melee. They retreat if two fall.

mapping.name: Nefru-Sekhem's Guard
mapping.setup: Two massive warriors block the path, weapons ready. They fight to the death.
mapping.tactics: Nefru-Sekhem and Timzahi fight in tandem, covering each other's flanks. They target healers first.

mapping.name: The Efreet's Lair
mapping.setup: The efreet reveals itself, demanding tribute or combat. The temperature rises as flames dance in its eyes.
mapping.tactics: The efreet uses fireballs to control the battlefield, targeting groups. It picks off stragglers with flame touch. If reduced to half HP, it retreats to bargain.

mapping.name: Tunnel Ambush
mapping.setup: Screeching fills the narrow tunnels as ghul-birds swoop down from above.
mapping.tactics: The ghul-birds attack in waves, using the narrow tunnels to prevent the party from fighting effectively.

mapping.name: The Dodecaphage Encounter
mapping.setup: A massive, impossible creature blocks the passage. It has too many mouths, too many eyes, and it is very, very hungry.
mapping.tactics: The Dodecaphage uses its immense size to fill the corridor, forcing the party to fight in cramped conditions. It swallows targets whole.

mapping.name: Collapsing Ceiling
mapping.trigger: A pressure plate in the center of the hallway.
mapping.countermeasures: The pressure plate can be spotted with a DC 15 Perception check. It can be disabled with a DC 13 Investigation check.

mapping.name: Flame Jet
mapping.trigger: Opening a treasure chest triggers a burst of flame from the walls.

mapping.name: Pit Trap
mapping.trigger: A section of floor gives way under weight.

mapping.name: Arrival at the Island
mapping.beats:
1. The party's ship approaches the island at dawn.
2. They see the ruined palace rising from the jungle.
3. A warning: fresh footprints in the sand — someone else is here.
4. The gate stands ajar, inviting them in.

mapping.name: The Gate Hall Discovery
mapping.beats:
1. The party enters the grand hall, awestruck by its scale.
2. Faded murals tell the story of a vizier's rise and fall.
3. A ghostly voice whispers: 'Turn back... or join the feast eternal.'
4. Ibrahim the Drifted Lord approaches cautiously.

mapping.name: The Efreet's Revelation
mapping.beats:
1. The temperature rises as the party enters the Treasure Hall.
2. Flames dance in the shadows — the efreet reveals itself.
3. It demands tribute: 'Kneel, and I shall grant you riches beyond measure.'
4. If refused, it attacks with terrifying fury.

mapping.name: The Final Battle
mapping.beats:
1. The White Shark and his elite guards surround the party.
2. The efreet watches, amused, from its throne of gold.
3. The battle rages — friend and foe fall alike.
4. Victory: the treasure is claimed, but at what cost?

mapping.name: Reach the Palace
mapping.objective: Travel to the island and find the entrance to Uzrah's Palace.
mapping.secrets: The palace is not abandoned — the White Shark's crew has already claimed it.

mapping.name: Stop the White Shark
mapping.objective: Defeat or drive off the White Shark of Basra and his crew before they can claim the treasure.
mapping.secrets: The White Shark knows more about the palace than he lets on — he seeks a specific artifact.

mapping.name: Survive the Efreet
mapping.objective: Deal with the capricious efreet that haunts the palace. Befriend, banish, or destroy it.
mapping.secrets: The efreet was bound to the palace centuries ago. It can be freed — or bound tighter.

mapping.name: Claim the Treasure
mapping.objective: Find and claim the legendary treasure of Uzrah's Palace.
mapping.secrets: The treasure is not what it seems — it is both a blessing and a curse.

mapping.name: The History of Uzrah's Palace
pages: Uzrah's Palace was built centuries ago by a legendary vizier who served the sultan of a great desert kingdom. The palace was a marvel of architecture, with soaring towers and lush gardens.

The vizier was known for his wisdom and wealth, but also for his pride. He made a bargain with an efreet, trading his soul for eternal power. But the efreet betrayed him, trapping his spirit in the palace forever.
The palace fell into ruin after the vizier's death. The gardens withered, the towers crumbled, and the efreet remained, guarding the treasure that the vizier had hoarded.

mapping.name: The Legend of the Efreet
pages: The efreet that haunts Uzrah's Palace is not a ordinary fire spirit. It is ancient, powerful, and capricious — capable of granting wishes and destroying those who displease it.
Legend says that the efreet was once a djinni who fell in love with a mortal. When the mortal died, the djinni's grief turned to rage, and it became an efreet, burning everything it touched.
The efreet can be summoned with fire and gold, but it always demands a price. Those who try to trick it often find themselves burned.

mapping.name: The White Shark's Plan
pages: The White Shark of Basra is not a typical pirate. He is old, cunning, and has spent decades searching for Uzrah's Palace.
His plan is to distribute his treasure on the island, using the palace as a base of operations. But he secretly seeks the vizier's artifact — an item of immense power hidden somewhere in the palace.
The White Shark knows about the efreet and has prepared offerings to appease it. Whether he can control it is another matter.
**Secrets:** The White Shark's true goal is to bind the efreet to his will, using the vizier's artifact.

mapping.name: 99 Devils of Uzrah's Palace
pages: An Arabian Nights-inspired dungeon adventure for 4-6 players, set on a remote island where a pirate lord plans to distribute his treasure among the ruins of a legendary palace.
The palace was once home to a vizier who made a bargain with an efreet. Now the ruins are haunted by the efreet, filled with traps and monsters, and guarded by the White Shark's crew.
The party must navigate the ruins, deal with the efreet, and either claim the treasure or stop the White Shark's plans. The adventure features exploration, combat, and roleplaying opportunities.

## Contents

**Locations:** Uzrah's Palace, The Gate Hall, The Upper Level, The Lower Level, The Builder Tunnels, The Treasure Hall, The Banquet Hall

**NPCs:** The White Shark of Basra, Faruq Night-Eater, Nefru-Sekhem, Timzahi, Varazdat, Ibrahim the Drifted Lord, Keeper of Cups and Cushions, Debbi, Sangtarash the Mercenary, Rafiq the Pirate, Pirate Archer, Ropeburn the Pirate, Pirate Treasure Hauler, Tariq the Monkey, Rashid the Jackal, Hound of Ash Silk

**Monsters:** Cobra, Ghul-Bird, Dodecaphage, Death Chanter, Filcher, Hyena of Shiraz, Smothering Carpet, Twin-Maw Ghariq, Ufrayta, Zagrossian Lion

**Encounters:** Gate Hall Ambush, Upper Level Patrol, Nefru-Sekhem's Guard, The Efreet's Lair, Tunnel Ambush, The Dodecaphage Encounter

**Traps:** Collapsing Ceiling, Flame Jet, Pit Trap

**Scenes:** Arrival at the Island, The Gate Hall Discovery, The Efreet's Revelation, The Final Battle

**Quests:** Reach the Palace, Stop the White Shark, Survive the Efreet, Claim the Treasure

**Lore:** The History of Uzrah's Palace, The Legend of the Efreet, The White Shark's Plan

**Environmental Effects:** Efreet's Fire Aura, Crumbling Ruins, Haunted Halls

mapping.name: Efreet's Fire Aura
mapping.effect: The efreet radiates intense heat. Within 30 feet, the air shimmers and flames dance at the edges of vision.
mapping.mechanical_notes: Creatures within 30 feet of the efreet take 1d6 fire damage at the start of their turn. Fire-resistant creatures are immune.

mapping.name: Crumbling Ruins
mapping.effect: The palace is ancient and unstable. Dust falls from the ceiling, and stones shift underfoot.
mapping.mechanical_notes: Running or charging in the ruins requires a DC 10 Dexterity check or fall prone. Loud noises may trigger cave-ins (DM's discretion).

mapping.name: Haunted Halls
mapping.effect: The spirits of the palace's former inhabitants linger. Whispers echo, and shadows move on their own.
mapping.mechanical_notes: Creatures with the Haunted One background have advantage on saves against fear effects in the palace. Others must make a DC 12 Wisdom save when entering a new area or be frightened for 1 minute.

mapping.benefits: The creature has advantage on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of the creature allies is within 5 feet of the target and the ally is not incapacitated.

mapping.benefits: While the creature remains motionless, it is indistinguishable from a normal object.

mapping.name: Two Heads
mapping.description: The creature has two heads. Each head controls one attack. The creature has advantage on saving throws against being blinded, deafened, stunned, knocked unconscious, or killed outright if one head is destroyed.
mapping.benefits: The creature has two heads. Each head controls one attack. The creature has advantage on saving throws against being blinded, deafened, stunned, knocked unconscious, or killed outright if one head is destroyed.

mapping.name: Incorporeal Movement

mapping.benefits: The creature can move through other creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain. It takes 5 (1d10) force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.

mapping.name: Innate Spellcasting
mapping.description: The creature innate spellcasting ability is Wisdom (spell save DC 12). It can innately cast the following spells, requiring no material components: At will: minor illusion; 1/day each: major image, mirror image.
mapping.benefits: The creature innate spellcasting ability is Wisdom (spell save DC 12). It can innately cast the following spells, requiring no material components: At will: minor illusion; 1/day each: major image, mirror image.

mapping.name: Combat Reflexes
mapping.description: Never freezes; recovers from surprise faster than anyone around them.
mapping.benefits: Advantage on initiative rolls. You cannot be surprised while conscious.

mapping.name: High Pain Threshold
mapping.description: Wounds register as information, not as agony.
mapping.benefits: Advantage on saving throws against effects that would stun you, and you ignore the first point of exhaustion from injury.

mapping.name: Night Vision
mapping.description: Eyes that open wide in the dark of the palace corridors.
mapping.benefits: You can see in dim light within 60 feet as if it were bright light.

mapping.name: Ghazi Rank
mapping.description: Recognised standing among the holy warriors of the frontier.
mapping.benefits: Ghazi warriors and the faithful treat you as an officer; you can requisition shelter, food and a mount from any Ghazi house.

mapping.name: Magery
mapping.description: An innate channel to the arcane, formalised by long study.
mapping.benefits: You count as a spellcaster for items and effects that require one, and you learn one extra cantrip from your class list.

mapping.name: Weapon Bond (Broadsword)
mapping.description: The blade answers only to its owner.
mapping.benefits: You cannot be disarmed of your bonded broadsword while conscious, and you can summon it to your hand as a bonus action if it is within 60 feet.

mapping.name: Fit
mapping.description: Hard living has made the body efficient.
mapping.benefits: Advantage on saving throws against disease and exhaustion; you recover one extra Hit Die on a long rest.

mapping.name: Charisma
mapping.description: People simply want to agree with them.
mapping.benefits: Advantage on Charisma (Persuasion) checks made against a creature that is not hostile.

mapping.name: High Manual Dexterity
mapping.description: Fingers that work faster than the eye can follow.
mapping.benefits: Advantage on Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) checks and on checks made with thieves’ tools.

mapping.name: Talent (Street Smarts)
mapping.description: An instinct for the shape of a city and the people working it.
mapping.benefits: Advantage on Charisma (Deception) and Wisdom (Insight) checks made in an urban setting.

mapping.name: Trickster
mapping.description: Cannot leave a mark unpicked or a mark unplayed.
mapping.benefits: Once per short rest you may take the Help action as a bonus action by means of a distraction or ruse.

mapping.name: Danger Sense
mapping.description: Knows a heartbeat before the trap fires.
mapping.benefits: You are not surprised by traps or ambushes as long as you are not incapacitated, and you have advantage on saves against traps.

mapping.name: Acute Vision
mapping.description: Picks out a rider on a dune at two miles.
mapping.benefits: Advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight.

mapping.name: Talent (Survivor)
mapping.description: The desert has already tried and failed to kill them.
mapping.benefits: Advantage on Wisdom (Survival) checks, and you always find enough food and water for yourself in any terrain.

mapping.name: Forgettable Face
mapping.description: Nobody in the caravanserai can describe her afterwards.
mapping.benefits: Creatures that see you only briefly cannot describe or identify you later; Dexterity (Stealth) checks made in a crowd have advantage.

mapping.name: Hard to Kill
mapping.description: Has been left for dead more than once and disagreed.
mapping.benefits: Advantage on death saving throws.

mapping.name: Luck
mapping.description: Falls off a mast and lands in the rigging.
mapping.benefits: Once per short rest you may reroll one attack roll, ability check, or saving throw and take the new result.

mapping.name: Eidetic Memory
mapping.description: Reads a page once and keeps it.
mapping.benefits: You can recall perfectly anything you have read, seen or heard within the last month; advantage on Intelligence (History) and (Investigation) checks to recall information.

mapping.name: Psychic Guidance (Stone Missile)
mapping.description: The stones know where they are going.
mapping.benefits: Once per turn you may reroll a missed spell attack made with a stone or earth effect.

mapping.name: Digitologist Guild Rank
mapping.description: Standing in the guild of number-mages.
mapping.benefits: Guild houses in any large city will shelter you, and you may consult the guild library without fee.

mapping.name: Ambidexterity
mapping.description: Neither hand is the off hand.
mapping.benefits: You do not have disadvantage on attacks made with your off hand, and two-weapon fighting adds your ability modifier to the second attack.

mapping.name: Hard to Subdue
mapping.description: Refuses to go down quietly.
mapping.benefits: Advantage on saving throws against being knocked unconscious, grappled or restrained.

mapping.name: Fearlessness
mapping.description: Has already made peace with dying.
mapping.benefits: Advantage on saving throws against being frightened.

mapping.name: Light Sleeper
mapping.description: Wakes at a footfall on sand.
mapping.benefits: You gain the benefits of a long rest even while keeping watch, and you cannot be surprised while resting.

mapping.name: Good Reputation
mapping.description: The poor quarters know his name and it is a good one.
mapping.benefits: Advantage on Charisma checks made with common folk who have heard of you.

mapping.name: Bite
mapping.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 1 piercing damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 10 Constitution saving throw or take 3 (1d6) poison damage.

mapping.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 10 (2d6+3) bludgeoning damage.

mapping.name: Chant of Death
mapping.description: The death chanter chants a death incantation. Each creature within 30 feet must succeed on a DC 12 Wisdom saving throw or be frightened for 1 minute. A creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

mapping.name: Claws
mapping.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 4 (1d4+2) slashing damage.

mapping.name: Steal
mapping.description: The filcher attempts to steal an item from a creature within 5 feet. The target must succeed on a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw or have one item of the filcher's choice stolen. The filcher must have at least one free hand to use this ability.

mapping.name: Smother
mapping.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one willing creature or creature that is grappled by the carpet. The target is grappled (escape DC 13) and restrained, and begins to suffocate.

mapping.name: Engulf
mapping.description: The carpet moves up to its speed. While doing so, it can enter a Large or smaller creature's space. If the creature fails a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw, the creature is smothered by the carpet.

mapping.description: Melee Spell Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. Hit: 10 (3d6) necrotic damage. The target's hit point maximum is reduced by an amount equal to the damage taken.

mapping.name: Outlander
mapping.description: You grew up in the wilds far from civilisation — the deep desert, the salt flats, the highland pastures.

mapping.name: Control Flames
mapping.description:
Görüş alanındaki, en fazla 5 fitlik bir küpü dolduran doğal alevi hedef alırsın ve aşağıdaki etkilerden birini yaratırsın:

- Alevleri 5 fitlik küpü doldurana kadar büyütür ya da söndürene kadar küçültürsün.
- Alevlerin ışığını iki katına çıkarır ya da yarıya indirirsin; rengini de değiştirebilirsin.
- Alevleri 5 fite kadar hareket ettirirsin.
- Bir yanıcı maddeyi tutuşturur ya da söndürürsün.

Etkilerden biri seçildiğinde 1 saat boyunca sürer; bu süre içinde büyüyü yeniden yaparak aynı alevler üzerinde başka bir etki seçebilirsin. Uzrah Sarayı'nın ateş hizmetkârları bu cantrip'i mangalları ve lamba alevlerini yönetmek için kullanır.
